sentences.text: Fully grown individuals of this dinosaur ranged from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and weighed between 600 and 4000 kilograms.
It possessed very short but strongly built arms with hands adapted for powerful grasping.
The animal walked on its toes with its hind limbs held under its body and slightly flexed knees and ankles.
Plateosaurus exhibited strong developmental plasticity, with adult sizes varying significantly from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and 600 to 4000 kg in weight.
Due to the abundance of fossils in Swabia, Germany, Plateosaurus earned the nickname 'Swabian lindworm'.
This species commonly lived at least 12 to 20 years, though its maximum lifespan remains unknown.
The genus Plateosaurus was described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
The initial discovery of Plateosaurus fossils occurred in 1834 at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany.
More than 100 skeletons of Plateosaurus have been discovered, making it one of the best-known dinosaurs.
In 1837, von Meyer described the bones as belonging to a gigantic Saurian with massive and hollow limb bones, allied to Iguanodon and Megalosaurus.
Plateosaurus was an obligate biped because it lacked the ability to pronate its forelimbs.
The animal likely increased its speed by using higher stride frequencies generated by rapid and powerful limb retraction.
It possessed teeth with a crown width greater than the root width, creating a cutting edge similar to modern herbivorous or omnivorous reptiles.
No fossil of Plateosaurus has been found containing gastroliths in the stomach area.
Pathologies on the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200 are hypothesized to result from capture myopathy caused by getting trapped in mud.
Plateosaurus exhibited a growth pattern similar to sauropods but with variable rates and final sizes, likely due to environmental factors like food availability.
Complete Plateosaurus skeletons and large parts including hind limbs are preserved dorsal side up, similar to turtles found at the same sites.
Martin Sander confirmed Fraas's mud-miring hypothesis, finding that animals above a certain weight sank into mud that liquefied as they struggled to free themselves.
Analysis of rib articulation suggests Plateosaurus had a lung air volume of approximately 20 liters for an individual weighing 690 kilograms, or 29 ml/kg of body weight.
Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, often referred to as a prosauropod.
As of 2019, only three species of Plateosaurus are universally accepted as valid: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
There is no extended consensus on the taxonomy of Plateosaurus species.
It is debated whether Plateosaurus was the direct ancestor of sauropods.
Paul Barrett proposed that Plateosaurus was an omnivore that supplemented its herbivorous diet with small prey or carrion.
Until the 1980s, paleontologists debated whether prosauropods like Plateosaurus were carnivorous.
